title: Array Hole Elimination & Packed SMI Preserver
subtopicTitle: V8 Internals: Hidden Classes & Inline Caches
concept: V8 Array Elements Kinds: PACKED_SMI vs HOLEY_DOUBLE
problemStatement: Implement `compactAndPackSmiArray(sparseArray)` that detects and removes holes from a sparse array while ensuring all remaining values are strictly 31-bit signed Small Integers (SMIs), returning a dense contiguous array.
interviewTrap: A single arr[100] = 1 in an empty array causes V8 to permanently demote the array from PACKED_SMI_ELEMENTS to HOLEY_SMI_ELEMENTS. Once demoted to HOLEY, element reads must check the prototype chain for every hole.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: V8 assigns a Hidden Class (Map) to every object. Adding properties in different orders or using 'delete' splits the transition tree and degrades inline caches from Monomorphic (fastest) to Megamorphic (hash table lookup fallback).

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Explain the V8 Array Elements Kinds lattice (PACKED_SMI -> HOLEY_DOUBLE).
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: V8 tracks array contents via 'Elements Kinds': 1) `PACKED_SMI_ELEMENTS`: dense array of Small Integers (-2^31 to 2^31-1). 2) `PACKED_DOUBLE_ELEMENTS`: dense array containing floating point numbers. 3) `PACKED_ELEMENTS`: dense array containing objects/strings. 4) `HOLEY_*`: contains unassigned holes (`[1, , 3]`). Transitions are strictly ONE-WAY: once an array is demoted to HOLEY or DOUBLE, it can NEVER be promoted back to PACKED_SMI!

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why are HOLEY arrays significantly slower than PACKED arrays?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: When reading an index from a PACKED array, V8 does a simple bounds check and memory read. In a HOLEY array, if the slot is empty, V8 is forced to walk the prototype chain (`Array.prototype`, then `Object.prototype`) to verify whether a property with that numeric key was defined on the prototype!
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Connects array performance to prototype chain lookups.

realWorldUseCases.description: Keeping audio sample arrays in PACKED_SMI or using TypedArrays to prevent prototype chain walking during 44.1kHz audio synthesis.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const samples = new Float32Array(1024); // natively packed

howToExplain.opening: V8 classifies arrays into Elements Kinds based on element types and presence of holes, transitioning down a one-way lattice from fast PACKED_SMI to slow HOLEY_ELEMENTS.
keyPoints: PACKED_SMI is the fastest array kind (contiguous small integers).
Introducing a decimal demotes to DOUBLE; an object demotes to PACKED.
Creating holes (sparse arrays) forces prototype chain lookups on reads.
Transitions are strictly one-way and cannot be reversed.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Avoiding holes and type mixing in arrays ensures V8 compiles array loops into vectorizable C-like loops.
analogies: A paved road: driving on a packed road is fast; driving on a road full of potholes (holes) requires stopping and checking every bump.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating an array with new Array(3) and populating it via index: arr[0]=1, arr[2]=3.
commonMistakes.why: new Array(3) creates a HOLEY array immediately.
commonMistakes.correct: Use Array.from(), array literals, or push() to keep arrays PACKED.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why are TypedArrays (Float64Array, Int32Array) immune to Elements Kind demotions?
followUpDeepDive.answer: TypedArrays are backed by fixed raw contiguous binary buffers (`ArrayBuffer`), having zero prototype lookup overhead and impossible hole representation.
